title: Switched and Full-Duplex Ethernet
markdown:
A central **Switch** device (with visible port grid) sits in the
middle; eight stations radiate outward from it, each on its own line
to a switch port. Each station sits inside its own pink dashed "Domain"
cone — i.e., a switch gives every single station its own dedicated
collision domain (contrast with the shared-domain bus topology in
Figure 13.16a).

{{viz:0}}

### Full-Duplex Switched Ethernet

A central **Switch** device with five stations radiating outward. Each
connection is drawn as a pair of arrows labeled **Transmit** and
**Receive** (opposite directions on the same line), showing that in
full-duplex mode a station can send and receive simultaneously with no
collision — unlike the plain switched view, no domain
shading is drawn here; the emphasis is on the duplex Transmit/Receive
arrow pairs instead.

{{viz:1}}
